pool.text: The Johor-Riau Sultanate was split due to a dispute.
Chinese cultivators relocated to new lands in Johor Bahru on plantations.
A treaty was signed between Sultan Ali and Temenggong Ibrahim in Singapore.
Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim renamed Tanjung Puteri to Iskandar Puteri upon arrival.
The town was renamed Johor Bahru after the Temenggong died.
The Malay Peninsula railway extension was finished in Johor Bahru.
The Johor Zoo was built as the oldest zoo in Malaysia.
The Sultan Ibrahim Building was built by British architect Palmer and Turner.
Japanese forces under General Tomoyuki Yamashita invaded the town.
The town formed the major political party UMNO at the Istana Besar.
Johor Bahru continued as state capital after the Federation of Malaysia formed.
Johor Bahru was officially granted city status.
Johor Bahru Prison was closed down after operating for 122 years.
A historical building was demolished illegally by its owner.
The Astaka became the tallest building in the city.
Johor Bahru was ranked the world's 39th most visited city by international tourists.
Johor Bahru had a population of 858,118 as a state capital.
Johor Bahru was ranked 432nd globally in the Global City Lab report.
Johor Bahru was ranked as a global city with high living quality.
Johor Bahru is ranked the world's 20th most attractive city for businesses.
